According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On newsletter, Apple is working to make its upcoming non-AR smart glasses another health and fitness platform — though these features are unlikely to debut alongside the first-generation model launching next year.

As he reports, Apple had previously been developing the Vision Pro as a health platform. The company was reportedly working on a version of Fitness+ that could run on the headset, allowing users to watch workout videos, track movements, and complete Activity Ring goals within Apple's first spatial computing device.

The original plan also included some special body-tracking analytics features to differentiate it from devices like the iPad or Apple TV. However, due to the headset's weight issues, the company ultimately abandoned this approach:

Apple is now revisiting similar ideas for its upcoming smart glasses — though the form factor will need to be adjusted given the lack of a display.

Fitness Features on the Smart Glasses

Apple's specific plans for the smart glasses aren't yet clear, but we do know the company is actively recruiting talent for this effort. Quoting the report:

In my view, two features that come to mind include the Workout Buddy feature Apple introduced on the Apple Watch last year, as well as a heart rate sensor similar to the one first used in the AirPods Pro 3, which could potentially be embedded in the glasses. This combination could very well make the glasses a practical companion for runners.

The cameras could also be used for various activities, allowing the system to identify whether your movements are correct, thereby helping you improve your training performance.

Time will tell what features Apple ultimately delivers. As mentioned at the outset, these features are unlikely to appear with the first-generation model — so it may take a few more years before we see Apple's complete vision.
